quote: certain of the Sicilian horsemen felt a strong aversion to that service, as being severe and arduous
notes: Sicilian horsemen averse to African service are released by Scipio in exchange for equipping and training Roman substitutes (livy:en:29:1).

quote: restored their property to the Syracusans, partly by proclamation, and partly even by judgments pronounced against those who pertinaciously retained their unjust acquisitions
notes: Scipio enforces senate-granted restitution of Syracusan Greeks' property against Italian holders by edict and adjudication (livy:en:29:1).

quote: been driven out by the opposite faction, which had delivered up Locri to Hannibal
notes: Locrian exiles at Rhegium use ransomed artisans to conspire with Rome and betray the Locri citadel, reversing the rival faction's defection to Hannibal (livy:en:29:6).

quote: He inflicted punishment on the persons principally concerned, and gave their effects to the leaders of the other party
notes: After retaking Locri Scipio punishes the defection's ringleaders, transfers their property to the loyal faction, and remits the city's status to the senate (livy:en:29:8).

quote: not only were other temples violated, but even the treasures of Proserpine, which had never been touched through all ages
notes: Pleminius and his garrison plunder Locri and sack the untouched treasury of Proserpina's temple, a sacrilege Livy makes the root of the ensuing violence (livy:en:29:8).

quote: they made an attack upon the lieutenant-general, having first mutilated the lictors in a shocking manner
notes: Soldiers' factions fight over loot, Pleminius scourges the tribunes, and his own troops mutiny, mutilating the legate's nose and ears; Scipio's cognizance acquits Pleminius and chains the tribunes (livy:en:29:9).

quote: after lacerating them with every punishment which the human body could endure, put them to death
notes: Pleminius tortures the military tribunes to death, denies them burial, and kills Locrian nobles who had complained to Scipio (livy:en:29:9).

quote: if the Idaean Mother should be brought from Pessinus to Rome
notes: A Sibylline prophecy found by the decemviri, reinforced by Delphi, moves the senate to resolve on importing the Idaean Mother cult (livy:en:29:10).

quote: Quintus Caecilius Metellus was nominated dictator for holding the elections, by the consul in Bruttium
notes: With the sick consul unable to return, Q. Caecilius Metellus is named dictator to hold the elections and abdicates when they conclude; proposal at livy:en:29:10, nomination quoted at livy:en:29:11.

quote: The senate was occupied with the determination of a matter of no small importance, namely, who was the most virtuous man in the state
notes: The senate adjudges young Scipio Nasica the best man in the state to receive the Magna Mater, who is installed in the temple of Victory with the new Megalesian games (livy:en:29:14).

quote: the twelve Latin colonies which had refused to furnish soldiers to the consuls, Quintus Fabius and Quintus Fulvius
notes: The senate disciplines the twelve defaulting colonies with doubled levies, an annual one-per-thousand tax, and a Roman-style census, detaining their envoys until they comply (livy:en:29:15).

quote: the monies which had been contributed by private individuals, when he and Marcus Claudius were consuls, should now at length be repaid
notes: Laevinus moves repayment of citizens' wartime loans to the treasury; the senate decrees repayment in three instalments (livy:en:29:16).

quote: ten ambassadors of the Locrians, covered with filth, and in mourning, and extending branches of olive
notes: Ten Locrian suppliants prostrate themselves before the consuls in the comitium and are granted a senate hearing against Pleminius; their speech fills livy:en:29:17-18 (quote at livy:en:29:16).

quote: Pleminius should be conveyed to Rome in chains, and in chains plead his cause
notes: Fabius moves that Pleminius be tried in chains and that Scipio be recalled with his command abrogated; the vote stalls amid heated debate over Scipio's Greek habits (livy:en:29:19).

quote: the tribunes might direct to apprehend him, and bring him home in right of their most sacred authority
notes: On Metellus's motion the senate sends an extraordinary commission - praetor, ten deputies, two tribunes, and an aedile - to Locri, empowered to arrest even Scipio if implicated (livy:en:29:20).

quote: Pleminius, and as many as thirty-two persons with him, they condemned and sent in chains to Rome
notes: The commission restores the sacred money with expiation, returns Locrian liberty, laws, and property, and condemns Pleminius with thirty-two accomplices, sending them to Rome in chains (livy:en:29:21).

quote: Pleminius, however, died in prison, before the people had come to a determination respecting him
notes: Pleminius dies in prison before the people's verdict, while the commission's report vindicates Scipio and the senate votes him his crossing to Africa (livy:en:29:22).

quote: made an attempt, by means of certain persons whom he had corrupted by bribes, to set fire to the city in several places
notes: In Clodius Licinius's variant account Pleminius plots from prison to fire Rome to escape, and is consigned to the Tullianum by senate decree (livy:en:29:22).

quote: many of the Tuscan nobles, who had either themselves gone, or had sent others to Mago respecting the revolt of their states
notes: The consul Cornelius holds senate-decreed trials in Etruria, condemning nobles who intrigued with Mago, with absentees condemned in exile and their property confiscated (livy:en:29:36).

quote: Cneius Babius, tribune of the people, thinking this a favourable opportunity of advancing himself at their expense, summoned them both to trial before the people
notes: The censors Livius and Nero degrade each other's horse and Livius disfranchises thirty-four tribes, and the tribune Babius's attempted prosecution of both is quashed by the senate (livy:en:29:37).

quote: They established also a new tax out of the price of salt
notes: The censors institute a graduated salt tax, popularly read as Livius's revenge on the tribes that condemned him, earning him the surname Salinator (livy:en:29:37).

quote: They then received a census of the twelve colonies, which had never been done before
notes: The censors receive the first-ever census of the twelve colonies so their manpower and money resources stand in the public records, completing the enforcement decreed at livy:en:29:15 (quote at livy:en:29:37).
